contract.intent: Close the regression: the STRUCTURED CONCLUSION becomes a PRECONDITION of the close. One shared L1 derivation (Commands.conclusion(id): the latest claim per acceptance criterion, the checks, and the ACs left UNCLAIMED) feeds BOTH the card and a new `complete!` refusal — so a task cannot reach `completed` while its conclusion is unreviewable: every contract AC must carry a claim, and at least one check must have PASSED against a cited commit (a sha in evidence.commits[] — the bytes under review). The refusal is named, lists exactly what is missing, and writes nothing. The handler-side duplicate derivation is removed (the card renders the L1 read). NAMED, UNFIXED GAP of this slice: the FRAME completes tasks by appending `completed` directly (frame.ts), so a frame-run task can still close thin — its own follow-up.
acceptanceCriteria: ann complete! <id> refuses with a NAMED error and writes NOTHING when any contract AC has no claim (naming those ACs), and separately when no check is both result='pass' and bound to a cited commit (checks[].sha in evidence.commits[])

the precondition reads the SAME L1 derivation the card renders (Commands.conclusion) — so a card showing NO CLAIM RECORDED plus a close that succeeds for the same state is unrepresentable; the handler-side duplicate is gone

a compliant conclusion still completes (every AC claimed + a passing check bound to a cited commit); a claim recorded in a LATER evidence event counts; a passing check with a foreign or absent sha does NOT satisfy the rule

the full suite stays green with the fixtures updated to carry compliant conclusions (they become examples of the rule), the live journey's ann check/verify stay clean, committed with evidence; the frame bypass is recorded as the named follow-up
